items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: But I mean the old man that started Berklee College of Music, he was one of the first people that started something in the Boston area — Mr. Berk.

ctx.x: At that time, ’55, was there resistance in that Academy?

Oh most definitely. Most definitely. And it’s only really started to lighten up to a certain extent over the past few years. But I mean the old man that started Berklee College of Music, he was one of the first people that started something in the Boston area — Mr. Berk. And you see the behemoth that they’ve become. And I sometimes lament the fact that some of the direction I know that he wanted things to go had sort of been absorbed into a much broader range now so that it’s beyond Berklee’s — their modus…
Contemporary music, yeah. Which is cool.
